div: Overview Please see use instructions and information at https://sandialabs.github.io/InterSpec/tutorials/#enrichment-and-isotopics-by-nuclides-tool-sep-2025

div.p: On the relative efficiency chart, the shaded band around the fitted curve and the error bars on the data points are both 1-sigma. The point error bars are statistical only, while the band is the uncertainty of the fitted curve itself. The same convention is used by the "Isotopics from peaks" tool, and in the HTML reports this tool exports.
The Range type of each energy range (ROI) says how its lower and upper energies are used:

ul.li: Lines + peak width: they are the lowest and highest gamma lines the ROI must include (the same energy for a single line). The ROI extends below its lower line until that line's peak is covered to the given percent, plus a given number of FWHM of continuum, and likewise above its upper line. The peak width and shape come from the fit, so the same ROIs suit any detector resolution. The continuum on either side stops short of other peaks found in the spectrum, and ROIs whose peaks are close together are merged. A floating peak the ROI reaches is covered as fully as the ROI's own lines. The range actually fit is shown under the ROI's fields.
Fixed range: they are the ROI's limits, whatever the detector.

Split by lines: an ROI is made around each significant gamma line within them, as for Lines + peak width, with overlapping ones merged. An initial fit uses the lines at peaks found in the spectrum; the final fit uses the lines that fit predicts to be statistically significant.

div.p: How far a ROI extends past its lines (the Below and Above fields) defaults to values suited to the detector type, shown in grey; enter a value to override it for that ROI. (For example, CZT ROIs cover less of each peak below its line, where CZT's long tail is.) Changing a Lines + peak width ROI to another range type starts from the range it was last fit over. Dragging the edge of a ROI on the chart makes it a fixed range; a ROI split by lines, or merged from several, becomes the individual fixed ROIs it was fit as. A continuum type of Auto chooses the continuum from how well each candidate describes the data after an initial fit.

The HTML, plain-text, CSV, etc. reports this tool produces — both in the GUI's "Export" menu and from the batch CLI (--file-report-template / --summary-report-template) — are rendered from Inja templates that consume a JSON data model built from the fit solution. You can add your own templates by creating a sub-directory named IsotopicsByNuclidesReportTmplts inside the app's user data directory (see Help→About InterSpec...→Data for this location) and dropping .tmplt.* files into it. Templates placed there become available to the batch CLI by filename.

A complete field reference and authoring guide is shipped at InterSpec_resources/static_text/IsotopicsByNuclidesReportTmplts/README.md. It is written specifically to be pasted into a web-based AI chatbot (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, etc.) along with a plain-English description of the report you want; the chatbot will produce a complete Inja template that you can save into the IsotopicsByNuclidesReportTmplts/ directory above. You can also start from one of the bundled templates in the same directory (std_rel_eff_summary.tmplt.html, std_rel_eff_summary.tmplt.txt, or std_multi_file_summary.tmplt.html) and modify it.
